facts.raw_span: 2 days of left orbital pain
hypertension controlled with lisinopril
several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/400 OS
Edematous, hyperemic left eyelids
Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Normal intraocular pressure
Normal fundi on both sides
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains; later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes
Increased abscess size with globe compression
diffusion-weighted imaging showed acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve

scope_out: orbital pain without optic nerve involvement

families.label: Optic Nerve Disorders
scope_out: orbital pain without optic nerve involvement

concepts.why: The patient has a history of epiphora and the imaging studies show a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess.
The patient presents with edematous, hyperemic left eyelids and diffuse limitation in extraocular movements, consistent with orbital cellulitis.
The patient has decreased visual acuity in the left eye and diffusion-weighted imaging shows acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve.
The initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes.
The imaging studies show a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding.
The patient has a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with increased abscess size and globe compression.
The patient has a history of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis, suggesting chronic dacryocystitis.
The patient has decreased visual acuity in the left eye and diffusion-weighted imaging shows acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve, without a clear cause.

rationales.F01: Left orbital pain is a non-specific symptom that could be related to several conditions, including orbital cellulitis.
rationales.F03: Epiphora without prior dacryocystitis suggests a possible blockage of the nasolacrimal duct, which could be related to a lacrimal sac abscess or chronic dacryocystitis.
rationales.F04: Decreased visual acuity in the left eye suggests an issue with the eye itself, such as optic neuritis or a complication of orbital cellulitis.
rationales.F05: Edematous and hyperemic left eyelids are indicative of an inflammatory process, such as orbital cellulitis or a lacrimal sac abscess.
rationales.F06: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements suggests an orbital process, such as orbital cellulitis or an orbital abscess, that is affecting the extraocular muscles.
rationales.F09: A left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding is highly suggestive of an infectious process, such as orbital cellulitis or a lacrimal sac abscess.
rationales.F10: The presence of Streptococcus pyogenes in cultures suggests a bacterial infection, which could be related to orbital cellulitis or a lacrimal sac abscess.
rationales.F11: Increased abscess size with globe compression suggests a severe infectious process, such as orbital cellulitis or an orbital abscess, that requires prompt treatment.
rationales.F12: Acute injury to the orbital segment of the left optic nerve, as shown by diffusion-weighted imaging, suggests an optic neuritis or a complication of orbital cellulitis.
